mechanism_narrative: The steady four-week rise in TRANSIT from -67.0 to -57.0 indicates that commuter and leisure mobility is recovering, which will lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose 10.0 points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than its last 28-day mean (-17.9) while TRANSIT remains above -60.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-week fall in PARKS greater than 15 points signals outdoor avoidance, pushing recreation demand indoors and raising RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls more than 15 points from t-1w to t-0w
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS dropped 20.9 points from -16.1 at t-1w to -37.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: Following a PARKS drop greater than 15 points week-on-week, RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is not higher than its last 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Improvement in WORKPLACES together with recovery in TRANSIT signals restored commuting and will pull RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.

evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose 8.3 points and TRANSIT rose 1.6 points from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: When WORKPLACES improves more than 5 points and TRANSIT improves more than 1 point week-on-week, RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than its last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: The onset of the late-November holiday shopping season will raise RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks, operating independently of commuting and school routines.
